source.rationale: THE DEFECT, CAPTURED. Live exec 13868196 (2026-08-25T10:09Z, 9qVyfUxmRQqrpGRMDLRuz, spine @177ddf3f): the customer widened a picker choice with "all", both picked customers carried their debtor code as canonical_code (parser raw "DELUXE HOME CENTRE SDN BHD (SETAPAK)" / "... - ACC 2", canonical 300-D059 / 300-D058). resolve-entity is sent `canonical_code ?? raw`, so resolutions[].token IS the debtor code, and the search-scope header's _axisWords path 1 quoted it through _rawOfTok - whose map was keyed on each entity's RAW only, so 300-D059 matched nothing, fell through unchanged, and the recorded reply opened with "Customer: 300-D059, 300-D058" - internal debtor codes in customer copy. `expected` is deliberately NOT the recorded output: the ONLY line changed is that header line, which now reads the two entities' raws in entity order ("Customer: DELUXE HOME CENTRE SDN BHD (SETAPAK), DELUXE HOME CENTRE SDN BHD - ACC 2"). Everything below it - the order list, the footer, and every `variables` field (where the codes are session data, not customer copy) - is byte-identical to the recording. The fix keys the _tokKey/_entByTok map under each entity's canonical_code as well as its raw, mirroring exactly what resolve-entity sends. 4th instance of resolver-token != entities[].raw (see memory resolver-token-is-not-entity-raw); Stage A fix 6 implemented the transform incompletely.
